entry.title: DYNAS: A Dynamic Network Penetration Testing Framework Using Deep Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
As network scale and uncertainty complicate automated penetration testing, reinforcement learning (RL) environments must support controlled evaluation under defensive and non-stationary conditions. We present DYNAS (Dynamic Network Attack Simulator), which combines parameterized large-scale scenario generation with stateful intrusion detection responses, explicit scan false-positive and false-negative noise, temporary service unavailability, and duration-based action timeouts. We further introduce Pen-DHRL, a recurrent manager--worker policy that selects persistent subgoals using IDS-conditioned global context.

Source: arXiv Systems & Architecture (cs.OS, cs.AR, cs.NI, cs.PF) · Tags: #computer-architecture #kernel-os #cryptography #ml-theory

entry.title: RV2GC: Reconstructing the Garbling Boundary in a RISC-V Garbled Processor
entry.summary:
Programmable garbled-circuit execution must balance the benefits of cross-program reuse against the cost of repeated work during secure execution. A complete garbled processor provides a fixed circuit for many programs, but its evaluator repeatedly visits processor-wide structures even when only a small part performs the current protected computation. We present RV2GC, which reconstructs the garbling boundary around a fixed library of RISC-V instruction circuits.

Source: arXiv Systems & Architecture (cs.OS, cs.AR, cs.NI, cs.PF) · Tags: #computer-architecture #kernel-os #cryptography #semiconductors

entry.title: Systematic Evaluation of Adversarial Jailbreaking Attacks and Defenses Across Seven Large Language Models
entry.summary:
Large language models (LLMs) deployed in safety-critical settings must resist adversarial inputs designed to elicit harmful outputs. We present a systematic empirical evaluation of five adversarial jailbreaking attack families---direct requests, roleplay-based jailbreaking, hypothetical framing, instruction override, and obfuscation---across seven open-weight and API-accessible LLMs: Llama-3-8B, Llama-3.1-8B, Llama-3.2-3B, Mistral-7B, Qwen2.5-7B, Gemma2-9B, and Phi-4-14B. We further evaluate four defense mechanisms: keyword blacklisting, self-reminder prompting, paraphrase-based sanitization, and perplexity-based filtering against the two most vulnerable models.

Source: arXiv Cryptography & Security (cs.CR) · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #infosec

entry.title: Package managers have an integrity problem
entry.summary:
I tested 25 of the most popular package managers to check whether they detect a compromised package repository injecting malicious code into legitimate packages. This code integrity problem could be solved using cryptographic hashes or signatures, but many package managers are still vulnerable to this threat. Of the 25 package managers reviewed 1 , fewer than half used lockfiles that checked for tampering by default, and only two verified the integrity of every package they downloaded.

Source: Trail of Bits Security Research · Tags: #infosec #cryptography #rust #databases

entry.title: SoK: Multiple Concurrent Proposer Blockchains. Multiple concurrent proposer (MCP) protocols let several parties contribute transactions to the same ledger update.
entry.summary:
Multiple concurrent proposer (MCP) protocols let several parties contribute transactions to the same ledger update. They can distribute communication and reduce one proposer's control over inclusion and order, but these benefits depend on how the contributions are combined. We describe a common architecture from transaction receipt through proposal formation, agreement, data recovery, ordering, execution, and state finality.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp

entry.title: Just How Secure is SRP, Really?
entry.summary:
An asymmetric Password-Authenticated Key Exchange (aPAKE) protocol allows a client and a server to agree upon a cryptographic key, with the only information shared in advance being a low-entropy password (memorized by the client) and a corresponding password file (stored in the server). The standard security definition for aPAKE is in the Universally Composable (UC) framework. Since aPAKE does not rely on a PKI, such protocols have received much attention in recent years due to their potential of replacing the traditional “password-over-TLS” approach for client-server authentication on the Internet.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #combinatorics

entry.title: Highly Efficient and Round-Optimal Asymmetric PAKE
entry.summary:
An asymmetric Password-Authenticated Key Exchange (aPAKE) protocol allows a client, who holds a raw password, and a server, who holds a one-way mapping of the password, to jointly establish a cryptographically strong session key, without an authenticated channel. The standard security definition for aPAKE is in the Universal Composability (UC) framework. Despite its great potential of being used in practice, existing aPAKE protocols are either not round-optimal, computationally inefficient, or not proven secure.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #combinatorics

entry.title: MinMandate: Task-Hiding Payment Authorization for Web Agents. AI agents increasingly pay for Web services on behalf of their users to complete complex tasks.
entry.summary:
AI agents increasingly pay for Web services on behalf of their users to complete complex tasks. Such a task needs many payments, and the user usually must approve each one, forcing the agent to stop at every payment. Mechanisms such as the Agent Payments Protocol (AP2) therefore enable the user to sign one payment mandate in advance that bounds the agent's payments for the task.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #agents

entry.title: Exact Error Bootstrapping and Comb Bootstrapping in FHEW/TFHE. In FHEW and TFHE, bootstrapping evaluates the decryption function via a blind rotation, whose resolution limits the message space.
entry.summary:
In FHEW and TFHE, bootstrapping evaluates the decryption function via a blind rotation, whose resolution limits the message space. We propose instead to bootstrap the \emph{error}. By rounding the ciphertext at a resolution that is a multiple of the message modulus, we preserve the message exactly.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp

entry.title: Complexity Analysis and Security Implications of the New Isogeny-Path Algorithm
entry.summary:
Very recently, Wesolowski (ePrint 2026/1486) proposed a novel heuristic algorithm for solving the supersingular isogeny-path problem in time and memory $p^{1/3+o(1)}$, where $p$ is the characteristic of the underlying field. Although this improves asymptotically on the previous $p^{1/2}\log^{O(1)}(p)$ complexity, its concrete impact on isogeny-based schemes, particularly SQIsign, remains unclear because of the superpolynomial overhead hidden in $p^{o(1)}$ and the exponential memory requirement. In this work, we assess the cost of Wesolowski's attack, study its time--memory tradeoffs, and investigate optimizations based on the van Oorschot -- Wiener (vOW) technique.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp
